name: stock-analysis
description: Produce a rigorous, sector-relative, multi-factor fundamental analysis of a publicly listed company — Indian (NSE/BSE) or US/global. Use when the user asks to analyse, research, evaluate, or value a stock, ticker, or listed company; asks whether a business is fundamentally strong, cheap, or expensive; compares companies or benchmarks one against its sector; or mentions OPM, ROCE, ROE, ROIC, P/E, EV/EBITDA, free cash flow, NIM, GNPA, CASA, promoter holding or pledging. Use it for accounting-quality and forensic questions — "is the profit real", "why is profit rising but cash isn't", auditor qualifications, related-party concerns — which route to the forensic-only mode, and for IPOs and not-yet-listed companies — "should I apply to this IPO", DRHP/RHP or S-1 questions, price band, grey market premium — which route to the IPO mode. Use it even when the request sounds casual ("is Infosys any good?"). Do not use it for personalised investment advice, portfolio allocation, or trading signals.

name: stock-correlation
description: Analyze how stocks move together using Yahoo Finance price history (yfinance): find correlated peers for a ticker, measure correlation, beta, and spread between specific tickers, cluster a group into a correlation matrix, and track rolling or regime-dependent correlation. Use this skill whenever the user asks what moves with a stock, what else drops when it drops, related tickers or sympathy plays, sector or supply-chain peers, pair trading or hedging pairs, beta or relative performance, correlation matrices, co-movement, or rolling/realized correlation — including well-known pairs like AMD/NVDA, GOOGL/AVGO, or LITE/COHR. With a single ticker, assume the user wants its correlated peers.

name: stock-liquidity
description: Analyze how liquid a stock is using Yahoo Finance data (yfinance): bid-ask spreads, volume and dollar volume (ADTV), top-of-book and options depth, square-root market impact and slippage estimates, turnover ratio, and Amihud illiquidity, rolled into a liquidity grade. Use this skill whenever the user asks about liquidity or trading costs — how easily a position can be entered or exited, what a large order would do to the price, spread or execution-cost estimates, order book depth, volume patterns, or liquidity comparisons — especially for small caps, penny stocks, and thinly traded names.

name: stocks
description: Stock quotes, history, search, compare, crypto via Yahoo.

name: stress-test
description: /em:stress-test — Business assumption stress testing. Use before betting on a plan whose core assumptions are unvalidated — e.g. stress-testing 'enterprise buyers will tolerate a 6-month pilot' or a hockey-stick revenue model.

name: study-plan
description: Build a weekly and daily study schedule from the goal and the available time, with method notes and adjustment rules, delivered as an Excel workbook

name: survey-analyst
description: Clean raw survey responses, run cross-tabulations and charts, and produce an analysis workbook plus a findings report, delivered as an Excel workbook and a Word document

name: tag-taxonomy
description: Apply and maintain the wiki's controlled tag vocabulary. Use for choosing, normalizing, auditing, or extending tags when creating or updating wiki pages; consult the taxonomy before assigning tags.

name: tax-season-organizer
description: Prepares tax-season materials for the owner's accountant, not tax advice. US federal tax; a non-US business gets its closed-books packet instead. Two modes: (1) quarterly estimated tax from YTD net income in the ledger (MYOB, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, or Zoho Books); (2) year-end 1099 prep, scanning the ledger, PayPal, and Stripe for contractors paid over USD 600 into a 1099-NEC list with missing W-9 flags.

name: trader-analyst
description: The Earnings Analyst. Reads a company's reported numbers straight from SEC EDGAR (XBRL company facts from its 10-Qs and 10-Ks, plus the latest earnings 8-K and its press release) and sums up what changed: revenue, gross, operating and net margins, net income and diluted EPS, quarter by quarter, each against the same quarter a year earlier, with the trailing twelve months. Reads an earnings call transcript when you paste one. Use when the user says "how did Tesla's earnings look", "analyze the earnings", "what changed this quarter", "is revenue growing", "check the 10-Q", "compare margins", "sum up the call", "does it report this week", or before trading a stock around its earnings.

name: trader-news
description: News Monitor. Tracks breaking news on every stock you watch and flags what moves it: Yahoo Finance headlines per ticker, each company's 8-K filings on SEC EDGAR (earnings, CEO changes, deals, restatements, bankruptcy) and how far each stock is from yesterday's close. Shows only what is new since the last check, newest first, in New York time, tags each item (earnings, analyst, deal, halt, regulatory, macro...) and never repeats one. Use when the user says "any news on TSLA", "why is this moving", "what's the news on my watchlist", "morning briefing", "pre-market news", "monitor the news", "did anything break", "check the 8-Ks", or after /trader-scanner finds setups.

name: trader-screener
description: The Stock Screener. Checks a list of companies against the user's own rules (revenue growth, margins, EPS, P/E, earnings yield, sector, anything in the metrics file), says exactly which rule each company passes or fails and by how much, and ranks the ones that pass into a shortlist. Reads the metrics /trader-analyst writes from SEC filings, or any CSV. Use when the user says "screen for stocks", "find me companies that", "filter my watchlist", "which of these pass my rules", "shortlist candidates", "rank these stocks", or "growing companies under 30 times earnings".

name: trader-tax
description: Tax Optimizer. Tracks cost-basis lots for every position (FIFO, highest cost first, or specific lots), shows unrealized gains and losses by lot with short or long term, works out what a sale would realize before you sell, finds tax-loss harvesting candidates over a loss threshold, checks the wash sale rule (30 days before and after, GOOG and GOOGL as one family), and writes harvest sells only as proposals. Not tax advice. Use when the user says "what are my gains", "cost basis", "tax lots", "tax-loss harvest", "what would selling cost me in tax", "short or long term", "wash sale", or before selling anything.

name: variance-analysis
description: Decompose financial variances into drivers with narrative explanations and waterfall analysis. Use when analyzing budget vs. actual, period-over-period changes, revenue or expense variances, or preparing variance commentary for leadership.

name: wave-accounting-automation
description: Wave Accounting toolkit is not currently available as a native integration. No Wave-specific tools were found in the Composio platform. This skill is a placeholder pending future integration.

name: wave_accounting-automation
description: Automate Wave Accounting tasks via Rube MCP (Composio): invoices, customers, payments, and small business accounting. Always search tools first for current schemas.

name: write-spec
description: Write a feature spec or PRD from a problem statement or feature idea. Use when turning a vague idea or user request into a structured document, scoping a feature with goals and non-goals, defining success metrics and acceptance criteria, or breaking a big ask into a phased spec.

name: yfinance-data
description: Fetch financial and market data with the yfinance Python library (Yahoo Finance). Use this skill whenever the user wants stock data: current quotes and price history, financial statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow), options chains, dividends and splits, earnings and analyst estimates, price targets and ratings, institutional and insider holdings, news, multi-ticker comparisons, stock screens, or sector and industry data. Use it even when the user gives only a ticker symbol (AAPL, MSFT, TSLA) and the intent has to be inferred. For earnings previews or recaps, estimate revisions, valuation, correlation, liquidity, or ETF premium analysis, prefer the dedicated skill.

name: zoho-books-automation
